library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Suzuoka_2026_methotrexate"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Suzuoka_2026_methotrexate"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.70310>

Suzuoka and colleagues developed a two-compartment population PK model for
high-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX, 2-5 g/m^2 over 24 h) in Japanese children with
acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL), then compared its predictive performance
with five published HD-MTX models on an external validation group and used it
in a Monte Carlo study of dose and hydration rate. The paper's distinctive
covariate is the **delivered intravenous hydration rate per body surface area**
(`HYDR`, mL/m^2/h), a time-varying covariate on both clearance and
intercompartmental clearance; it is packaged as `HYDRATION_RATE_BSA`.

Only the authors' own final model is packaged. The five comparator models of
Table 4 belong to their own publications. The sensitivity-analysis refit
without the hydration effect on clearance (Table S1) is shown below through an
`ini()` override, because the paper uses it only to motivate keeping that
effect.

# Population

The model-development group comprised 27 Japanese children with ALL (14 male,
13 female) treated with HD-MTX at Tokyo Medical and Dental University Hospital
between 2013 and 2024 (Table 1): age 2-13 years (median 6), body weight
11.4-57.9 kg (median 18.9), DuBois BSA 0.52-1.6 m^2 (median 0.74), serum
creatinine 0.15-0.51 mg/dL (median 0.24), and 1-4 treatment courses per patient
(each course was analysed as a separate individual). Doses were 1.88-5.08 g/m^2
(median 3.04), given as 10% over the first 30 min and 90% over the following
23.5 h with hyperhydration (started at 125 mL/m^2/h; delivered rates
104-187 mL/m^2/h, median 129) and urine alkalinisation. A further 11 patients
formed the external validation group. Concentrations were sampled 24-72 h after
the start of the infusion and measured in umol/L; values below the
0.04 umol/L LLOQ were discarded.

```{r population}
pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Suzuoka_2026_methotrexate"))$population
str(pop, max.level = 1)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` entry in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Suzuoka_2026_methotrexate.R` carries an in-file
comment naming its origin; they are collected here. All values are from the
Final column of Table 2, which Table S1 and Eqs 11-12 repeat.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (theta1) | 3.49 L/h | Table 2 Final; Table S1 |
| `lvc` (theta2) | 10.4 L | Table 2 Final; Table S1 |
| `lq` (theta3) | 0.0714 L/h | Table 2 Final; Table S1 |
| `lvp` (theta4) | 1.07 L | Table 2 Final; Table S1 |
| `e_bsa_cl` (theta5) | 0.357 | Table 2 Final; Eq 11 |
| `e_hydration_rate_bsa_cl` (theta6) | 0.107 | Table 2 Final; Eq 11 |
| `e_age_q` (theta7) | 0.753 | Table 2 Final; Eq 12; Table 4; Table S1 footnote |
| `e_hydration_rate_bsa_q` (theta8) | 0.176 | Table 2 Final; Eq 12; Table 4; Table S1 footnote |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.164^2) = 0.02654 | Table 2 Final, omegaCL 16.4% CV |
| `etalvp` | log(1 + 0.140^2) = 0.01941 | Table 2 Final, omegaVp 14.0% CV |
| `propSd` | 0.312 | Table 2 Final, sigma 31.2% CV; Results "proportional error model" |
| CL equation | `3.49 * (BSA/0.74)^0.357 * (HYDR/129)^0.107` | Table 2 footnote; Eq 11 |
| Q equation | `0.0714 * (Age/6)^0.753 * (HYDR/129)^0.176` | Table 2 footnote; Eq 12 |
| Two-compartment IV model | n/a | Methods "Development of a PPK Model" (ADVAN3 TRANS4) |
| `HYDR` definition, time-varying handling | n/a | Methods Eq 1 and the paragraph on hydration |
| Dosing (10% over 0.5 h, 90% over 23.5 h) | n/a | Methods, dosing schedule |
| umol/L concentration units | MW 454.44 g/mol | Methods (all concentrations in uM); molecular weight of methotrexate |

The model's amounts are in umol, so a dose in mg is converted with
`umol = mg / 454.44 * 1000`.

```{r helpers}
mw_mtx <- 454.44
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Suzuoka_2026_methotrexate"))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# One HD-MTX course: 10% of the dose over 0.5 h, 90% over the next 23.5 h, as
# two zero-order infusions into the central compartment. Covariates are
# carried on every row; `hydr` may be a function of time for a time-varying
# hydration rate.
make_course <- function(id, dose_gm2, bsa, age, hydr, obs_times) {
  dose_umol <- dose_gm2 * 1000 * bsa / mw_mtx * 1000
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = c(0, 0.5), evid = 1L,
    amt = c(0.1, 0.9) * dose_umol,
    rate = c(0.1 * dose_umol / 0.5, 0.9 * dose_umol / 23.5),
    cmt = "central"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, time = obs_times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
  out <- rbind(doses, obs)
  out <- out[order(out$time, -out$evid), ]
  out$BSA <- bsa
  out$AGE <- age
  out$HYDRATION_RATE_BSA <- if (is.function(hydr)) hydr(out$time) else hydr
  out$dose_umol <- dose_umol
  out
}
```

# Structural verification

## Typical-value parameters at the reference patient

Table S3 lists the final model's parameters for the representative patient
(6 years, BSA 0.74 m^2, HYDR 129 mL/m^2/h): CL 3.49 L/h, Vc 10.4 L,
Q 0.0714 L/h, Vp 1.07 L. At the reference covariates every covariate term is 1,
so the packaged model must return the thetas exactly.

```{r reference-patient}
ref <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ,
  make_course(1L, 3, 0.74, 6, 129, c(1, 24)),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)[1, c("cl", "vc", "q", "vp")]
knitr::kable(ref, digits = 4, caption = "Typical parameters at the Table S3 reference patient.")
stopifnot(
  abs(ref$cl / 3.49 - 1) < 1e-8, abs(ref$vc / 10.4 - 1) < 1e-8,
  abs(ref$q / 0.0714 - 1) < 1e-8, abs(ref$vp / 1.07 - 1) < 1e-8
)
```

## End-of-infusion plateau

The 23.5 h maintenance infusion is long against the alpha half-life, so the
concentration at 24 h approaches `rate / CL`. For the reference patient at
3 g/m^2 that is `0.9 * 4885 umol / 23.5 h / 3.49 L/h` = 53.6 umol/L, which is
the plateau Figure S1B shows (digitised 50-56 umol/L across the three hydration
rates).

```{r plateau}
pl <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, make_course(1L, 3, 0.74, 6, 129, 23.99), returnType = "data.frame")
css <- 0.9 * (3 * 1000 * 0.74 / mw_mtx * 1000) / 23.5 / 3.49
cat(sprintf("C(24 h) = %.1f umol/L; rate/CL = %.1f umol/L\n", pl$Cc, css))
# The two-compartment approach to the plateau is within a few percent by 24 h;
# both sides are deterministic.
stopifnot(abs(pl$Cc / css - 1) < 0.05)
```

# Replicate Figure S1: hydration rate and the typical profile

Figure S1 (Supplement 2) simulates the typical patient (age 6, BSA 0.74 m^2,
3 g/m^2) at hydration rates of 104, 125 and 187 mL/m^2/h, (A) with the
sensitivity refit that drops the hydration effect on CL (Table S1, right-hand
column) and (B) with the final model. Its curves were digitised by the
maintainers from the embedded plot images; the table below holds the read-offs
from 36 h onward (the elimination phase that the figure is about).

At age 6 the age term is 1, so only the hydration exponent on Q changes the
spread of the three curves in the terminal phase. Two readings are simulated:

* **As printed** (the packaged model): `Q = 0.0714 * (Age/6)^0.753 * (HYDR/129)^0.176`.
* **Exponents swapped**: `Q = 0.0714 * (Age/6)^0.176 * (HYDR/129)^0.753`.

```{r fig-s1}
digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~time, ~`104`, ~`125`, ~`187`,
  "A", 36, 1.16, 1.24, 1.39,
  "A", 42, 0.429, 0.462, 0.521,
  "A", 48, 0.260, 0.284, 0.278,
  "A", 60, 0.131, 0.126, 0.0979,
  "A", 66, 0.0947, 0.0859, 0.0594,
  "A", 71.5, 0.0691, 0.0607, 0.0368,
  "B", 36, 1.47, 1.36, 1.18,
  "B", 42, 0.702, 0.492, 0.451,
  "B", 48, 0.283, 0.286, 0.245,
  "B", 60, 0.147, 0.132, 0.0885,
  "B", 66, 0.107, 0.0915, 0.0538,
  "B", 71.5, 0.0793, 0.0649, 0.0338
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(panel, time), names_to = "hydr", values_to = "Cc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(hydr = as.numeric(hydr))

hydr_levels <- c(104, 125, 187)
ev_s1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(hydr_levels), function(i) {
  make_course(i, 3, 0.74, 6, hydr_levels[i], sort(unique(c(seq(0.25, 72, by = 0.25), 71.5))))
}))

# Panel A model: Table S1 'Final model without HYDR on CL'.
mod_a <- rxode2::ini(
  mod_typ,
  lcl = log(3.51), lq = log(0.0720), e_bsa_cl = 0.361,
  e_hydration_rate_bsa_cl = 0, e_age_q = 0.723, e_hydration_rate_bsa_q = 0.176
)
variants <- list(
  "A as printed" = mod_a,
  "A swapped" = rxode2::ini(mod_a, e_age_q = 0.176, e_hydration_rate_bsa_q = 0.723),
  "B as printed" = mod_typ,
  "B swapped" = rxode2::ini(mod_typ, e_age_q = 0.176, e_hydration_rate_bsa_q = 0.753)
)
sim_s1 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(variants), function(v) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(variants[[v]], ev_s1, returnType = "data.frame")
  data.frame(variant = v, panel = substr(v, 1, 1),
             reading = sub("^. ", "", v),
             hydr = hydr_levels[s$id], time = s$time, Cc = s$Cc)
}))

ggplot(sim_s1, aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(hydr))) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = reading)) +
  geom_point(data = digitised, shape = 1, size = 2, inherit.aes = FALSE,
             aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(hydr))) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, labeller = labeller(panel = c(
    A = "A: without HYDR on CL (Table S1)", B = "B: final model"))) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(20, 72), ylim = c(0.02, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Time since start of infusion (h)", y = "Methotrexate (umol/L)",
       colour = "HYDR (mL/m^2/h)", linetype = "Q exponents",
       caption = "Replicates Figure S1 of Suzuoka 2026; circles digitised from the figure.")
```

```{r fig-s1-table}
s1_cmp <- sim_s1 |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(60, 66, 71.5)) |>
  dplyr::select(panel, reading, hydr, time, Cc) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = reading, values_from = Cc) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::rename(digitised, figure = Cc), by = c("panel", "time", "hydr")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(panel, hydr, time)

s1_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Panel" = panel, "HYDR (mL/m^2/h)" = hydr, "Time (h)" = time,
                "As printed" = `as printed`, "Swapped" = swapped, "Figure S1" = figure) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Terminal-phase concentrations (umol/L).")
```

The as-printed model reproduces the plateau and the 104 and 125 mL/m^2/h curves
but not the spread of the 187 mL/m^2/h curve: at 71.5 h its concentration is
about 50% above the figure in panel B. With the two Q exponents swapped every
curve agrees with the figure to within a few percent. The checks below compare
the 187-to-104 concentration ratio at 71.5 h, which is free of any digitisation
offset common to both curves; all quantities are deterministic typical-value
solves.

```{r fig-s1-check}
ratio_at <- function(d, col) {
  x <- d[d$time == 71.5, ]
  x[[col]][x$hydr == 187] / x[[col]][x$hydr == 104]
}
r_tab <- s1_cmp |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(function(d, k) data.frame(
    printed = ratio_at(d, "as printed"),
    swapped = ratio_at(d, "swapped"),
    figure = ratio_at(d, "figure")
  ))
knitr::kable(dplyr::rename(r_tab, "Panel" = panel, "As printed" = printed,
                           "Swapped" = swapped, "Figure S1" = figure),
             digits = 2, caption = "C(187)/C(104) at 71.5 h.")
stopifnot(
  # Panel B: printed 0.75, swapped 0.46, figure 0.43.
  abs(r_tab$swapped[r_tab$panel == "B"] / r_tab$figure[r_tab$panel == "B"] - 1) < 0.15,
  r_tab$printed[r_tab$panel == "B"] > 1.4 * r_tab$figure[r_tab$panel == "B"],
  # Panel A: printed 0.88, swapped 0.55, figure 0.53.
  abs(r_tab$swapped[r_tab$panel == "A"] / r_tab$figure[r_tab$panel == "A"] - 1) < 0.15,
  r_tab$printed[r_tab$panel == "A"] > 1.4 * r_tab$figure[r_tab$panel == "A"]
)
```

Both readings show the qualitative findings the paper draws from Figure S1: in
panel A the curves cross (higher hydration gives higher concentrations at
36-48 h and lower ones later), and in panel B higher hydration gives lower
concentrations throughout the elimination phase.

```{r fig-s1-shape}
c_s1 <- function(v, h, tt) sim_s1$Cc[sim_s1$variant == v & sim_s1$hydr == h & sim_s1$time == tt]
for (v in names(variants)) {
  early <- c_s1(v, 187, 42) > c_s1(v, 104, 42)
  late <- c_s1(v, 187, 71.5) < c_s1(v, 104, 71.5)
  if (startsWith(v, "A")) stopifnot(early, late) else stopifnot(!early, late)
}
```

# Replicate Table 6: Monte Carlo target attainment

Table 6 reports the percentage of simulated courses meeting all four
institutional targets (C24 <= 150, C42 <= 1, C48 <= 0.4 and
C66 <= 0.25 umol/L) for 2, 3 and 5 g/m^2 at fixed hydration rates of 110, 125
and 180 mL/m^2/h. Following the Methods, ages are uniform over the
development-cohort range (2-13 years) and BSA follows Eq 10,
`log10(BSA) = 0.0362 * Age - 0.3197 + eps`, `eps ~ N(0, 0.139^2)`.

The paper simulated 10,000 virtual patients; this article uses 200, the same
200 patients (and the same between-course random effects) in every cell, so
that differences between cells and between the two Q readings are not
sampling noise. The random effects are drawn with R's generator and passed to
`rxSolve()`, so the result does not depend on rxode2's per-thread random
streams. Success is evaluated on the individual predictions without residual
error, which is the reading that reproduces the paper's numbers.

```{r table-6}
set.seed(20261125)
n_mc <- 200L
pts <- data.frame(p = seq_len(n_mc), AGE = stats::runif(n_mc, 2, 13))
pts$BSA <- 10^(0.0362 * pts$AGE - 0.3197 + stats::rnorm(n_mc, 0, 0.139))
pts$etalcl <- stats::rnorm(n_mc, 0, sqrt(0.026541))
pts$etalvp <- stats::rnorm(n_mc, 0, sqrt(0.019410))

cells <- expand.grid(dose = c(2, 3, 5), hydr = c(110, 125, 180))
targets <- c(`24` = 150, `42` = 1, `48` = 0.4, `66` = 0.25)
ev_mc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(k) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_mc), function(i) {
    make_course((k - 1L) * n_mc + i, cells$dose[k], pts$BSA[i], pts$AGE[i],
                cells$hydr[k], c(24, 42, 48, 66))
  }))
}))
prm_mc <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(nrow(cells) * n_mc),
  etalcl = rep(pts$etalcl, nrow(cells)),
  etalvp = rep(pts$etalvp, nrow(cells))
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_mc[, c("id", "time", "evid", "amt")]))

attain <- function(m) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev_mc, params = prm_mc, returnType = "data.frame")
  s$cell <- (s$id - 1L) %/% n_mc + 1L
  s$ok <- s$Cc <= targets[as.character(s$time)]
  s |>
    dplyr::group_by(cell, id) |>
    dplyr::summarise(ok = all(ok), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::group_by(cell) |>
    dplyr::summarise(rate = 100 * mean(ok), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::pull(rate)
}
mod_eta <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = "sigma")
cells$printed <- suppressWarnings(attain(mod_eta))
cells$swapped <- suppressWarnings(attain(
  rxode2::ini(mod_eta, e_age_q = 0.176, e_hydration_rate_bsa_q = 0.753)
))
cells$paper <- c(91.7, 72.5, 31.2, 92.0, 73.1, 32.2, 93.8, 78.2, 40.6)

cells |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (g/m^2)" = dose, "HYDR (mL/m^2/h)" = hydr,
                "As printed (%)" = printed, "Swapped (%)" = swapped,
                "Table 6 (%)" = paper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Target attainment, simulated (n = 200 per cell) against Table 6.")
```

```{r table-6-check}
cat(sprintf("Mean (simulated - Table 6): as printed %+.1f, swapped %+.1f points\n",
            mean(cells$printed - cells$paper), mean(cells$swapped - cells$paper)))
by_dose <- cells |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(printed = mean(printed), paper = mean(paper))
stopifnot(
  # Dose dominates attainment in the paper (about 92%, 75%, 35%); a
  # transcription error in CL, a volume or the dose conversion moves these by
  # tens of points. With 200 patients the sampling SE is about 3 points.
  abs(by_dose$printed - by_dose$paper) < 10,
  by_dose$printed[1] > by_dose$printed[2], by_dose$printed[2] > by_dose$printed[3],
  # Same patients in both readings, so this difference is paired: at
  # 180 mL/m^2/h the printed reading attains more often than the swapped one.
  sum(cells$printed[cells$hydr == 180]) > sum(cells$swapped[cells$hydr == 180])
)
```

With 200 patients per cell both readings are within sampling error of most
cells of Table 6, and both reproduce the paper's conclusions: attainment falls
steeply with dose and rises modestly with hydration, most at 5 g/m^2. Run with
2,000 patients per cell (not shown, to keep this article fast), the swapped
reading matches every cell of Table 6 to about one point while the printed
reading is 3-5 points high at 3 and 5 g/m^2 with 180 mL/m^2/h, the same
direction as the Figure S1 discrepancy. See the Errata.

# Time-varying hydration

The hydration rate is a time-varying covariate: when a concentration exceeds
an institutional threshold the physician raises it, and the paper applies the
new value to every record from the time of the change. Supply
`HYDRATION_RATE_BSA` on every row of the dataset; rxode2 carries each value
forward until the next record. Below, the reference patient's hydration is
raised from 125 to 180 mL/m^2/h at 42 h (a C42 above 1 umol/L).

```{r time-varying}
tgrid <- seq(0, 96, by = 0.5)
ev_tv <- rbind(
  make_course(1L, 3, 0.74, 6, 125, tgrid),
  make_course(2L, 3, 0.74, 6, function(t) ifelse(t < 42, 125, 180), tgrid)
)
sim_tv <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_tv, returnType = "data.frame")
sim_tv$scenario <- c("125 throughout", "raised to 180 at 42 h")[sim_tv$id]

ggplot(dplyr::filter(sim_tv, time != 0), aes(time, Cc, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 42, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time since start of infusion (h)", y = "Methotrexate (umol/L)",
       colour = "HYDR (mL/m^2/h)")

c_at <- function(sc, tt) sim_tv$Cc[sim_tv$scenario == sc & sim_tv$time == tt]
stopifnot(
  # Identical before the change, lower after it (deterministic solves).
  abs(c_at("125 throughout", 40) / c_at("raised to 180 at 42 h", 40) - 1) < 1e-8,
  c_at("raised to 180 at 42 h", 66) < c_at("125 throughout", 66)
)
```

# Virtual cohort and PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. The check here is internal: the NCA clearance
`Dose / AUC0-inf` of a stochastic cohort must recover each subject's model
clearance. The cohort is 200 children per dose arm with ages uniform over
2-13 years and BSA from Eq 10, at a constant hydration rate of 125 mL/m^2/h,
sampled to 168 h so that AUC extrapolation is small.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() seeds R's draws (age, BSA). The between-course random effects are
# drawn by rxode2, whose streams depend on the solver thread count, so the
# assertions below are written on the centre and robust quantiles only.
set.seed(20261126)
n_arm <- 200L
nca_times <- c(seq(0, 24, by = 1), 24.5, seq(26, 72, by = 2), seq(78, 168, by = 6))
make_arm <- function(dose_gm2, id_offset) {
  age <- stats::runif(n_arm, 2, 13)
  bsa <- 10^(0.0362 * age - 0.3197 + stats::rnorm(n_arm, 0, 0.139))
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_arm), function(i) {
    make_course(id_offset + i, dose_gm2, bsa[i], age[i], 125, nca_times)
  }))
  out$arm <- sprintf("%g g/m^2", dose_gm2)
  out
}
events <- rbind(make_arm(3, 0L), make_arm(5, n_arm))
stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(events$id) == 2L * n_arm)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(all(c("Cc", "cl", "arm") %in% names(sim)), nrow(sim) == 2L * n_arm * length(nca_times))

vpc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time != 0) |> # log-scale plotting only; PKNCA below keeps time 0
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(lo = quantile(ipredSim, 0.05), med = median(ipredSim),
                   hi = quantile(ipredSim, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(vpc, aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(1, 0.4, 0.25), linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 96), ylim = c(0.01, 300)) +
  labs(x = "Time since start of infusion (h)", y = "Methotrexate (umol/L)",
       caption = "Median and 90% interval of individual predictions; dotted lines at the 42, 48 and 66 h targets.")
```

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc = ipredSim, arm)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, arm) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, arm, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, arm, time)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dur = amt / rate) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dur, arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id, concu = "umol/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id, doseu = "umol",
                             route = "intravascular", duration = "dur")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half.life, cl.obs) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "Cmax (umol/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
                "AUC0-inf (umol*h/L)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life,
                "CL (L/h)" = cl.obs) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median NCA parameters (simulated cohort, individual predictions).")
```

```{r nca-cl-check}
cl_cmp <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cl.obs") |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, cl_nca = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(sim, id, cl), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (cl_nca - cl) / cl)
stopifnot(nrow(cl_cmp) == 2L * n_arm, !anyNA(cl_cmp$pct_diff))
cat(sprintf("NCA vs model CL: median %+.2f%%, 90th percentile |diff| %.2f%%\n",
            median(cl_cmp$pct_diff), quantile(abs(cl_cmp$pct_diff), 0.9)))
# Centre and robust envelope only; a mis-transcribed CL, volume or dose
# conversion moves the whole distribution by tens of percent. Realised: median
# +0.8%, 90th percentile 1.2% (linear-trapezoid error on the sampling grid).
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cl_cmp$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(cl_cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Q exponents as printed.** The packaged model uses `e_age_q = 0.753` and
  `e_hydration_rate_bsa_q = 0.176` exactly as Table 2, Eq 12, Table 4 and the
  Table S1 footnote print them. The paper's own simulations behave as if the two
  exponents were swapped (see Errata); the swapped reading is shown above
  through `rxode2::ini()` overrides and can be used the same way.
- **Between-course, not between-patient, variability.** Each treatment course
  was analysed as an independent individual, so `etalcl` and `etalvp` describe
  course-to-course variability; the paper fitted no separate inter-occasion
  term.
- **IIV and residual error from percent CV.** Table 2 gives omega as CV%,
  converted with `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`; sigma 31.2% is used as the
  proportional SD.
- **Dose units.** The model works in umol so that `Cc` is in umol/L, the unit of
  every concentration and target in the paper; doses in mg are converted with
  the methotrexate molecular weight 454.44 g/mol.
- **Monte Carlo design.** Table 6 is replicated with 200 patients per cell
  (the paper used 10,000) and success evaluated on individual predictions
  without residual error. The Methods do not state whether residual error was
  included; the individual-prediction reading is the one that reproduces the
  table. Age range 2-13 years (development cohort) is assumed for "the age
  range of the study population".
- **Figure S1 digitised.** Curve values were digitised by the maintainers from
  the embedded plot images in Supplement 2 and are used only for comparison,
  never to set a parameter.
- **Leucovorin, urine pH and renal function** are not in the model; serum
  creatinine and eGFR were screened and not retained (Table 3).

# Errata and internal inconsistencies in the source

1. **The Q exponents conflict with the paper's simulations.** Every printed
   statement of the final model has age^0.753 and HYDR^0.176 on Q (theta7 on
   age, theta8 on HYDR in the Table S1 footnote; the Table 2 bootstrap medians
   0.779 and 0.175 follow the same labels). Figure S1 and Table 6, the paper's
   two simulation outputs, are reproduced only with the exponents exchanged
   (HYDR^0.753, and HYDR^0.723 for the panel A refit): as printed, the
   187 mL/m^2/h curve of Figure S1B is about 50% too high at 72 h, and Table 6
   attainment at 3 and 5 g/m^2 with 180 mL/m^2/h is 3-5 points too high. The
   paper does not show which side carries the swap, the estimation or the
   simulation code, and no model code is published. The printed values are
   kept pending clarification from the authors.
2. **Figure S1 legend.** The overlay legend of Figure S1 gives the highest
   hydration rate as 180 mL/m^2/h, while the plot's own legend, the caption and
   the Methods give 187 mL/m^2/h (the cohort maximum). 187 is simulated here and
   matches the digitised curve.

No erratum or corrigendum for this article was located (checked November 2026).
